name: Plain
verdict: No OAuth or approval is documented. Each customer admin creates a machine user and a least-privilege API key and shares it with you, about 1-3 days.
needGuide: No — just collect an API key from a machine user (Settings → Machine Users).

auth.detail: GraphQL API with Bearer API keys owned by machine users (Settings → Machine Users), each key with fine-grained permissions, shown once. Plain also has OAuth apps (authorization code, S256 PKCE, openid and offline_access scopes), but docs say the app works only in the workspace where it was created, so it is not a multi-tenant third-party flow.

approval.gate: None for API keys. No approval process, marketplace or cross-workspace OAuth is documented.

scopes.why: Permissions are chosen per key when it is created.
scopes.summary: Per-key permissions chosen at creation; error messages name missing permissions. OAuth apps expose only openid and offline_access in the docs.

cost: Requires a Plain workspace (paid plan or trial; not verified)
prerequisites: Account and owner: A Plain workspace member able to create machine users and API keys (the role needed is not stated).
Where you register: Customer workspace: Settings → Machine Users → + Add Machine User → create API key with chosen permissions. Own-workspace OAuth: Settings → OAuth applications → Add OAuth app.
Cost: Requires a Plain workspace (paid plan or trial; not verified)

registerAt.path: Customer workspace: Settings → Machine Users → + Add Machine User → create API key with chosen permissions. Own-workspace OAuth: Settings → OAuth applications → Add OAuth app.

steps.do: Add a connect screen asking for a Plain API key and explaining the permissions needed
Customer admin: Settings → Machine Users → + Add Machine User, name it for your app, create an API key with only the required permissions
Validate by calling the GraphQL API (e.g. myMachineUser) with Authorization: Bearer plainApiKey_xxx; read the permission names from any error
Store the key encrypted (shown only once) and support key rotation by adding a second key
Ask Plain whether multi-workspace OAuth is planned or available on request

roles.team: A Plain workspace member able to create machine users and API keys (the role needed is not stated).
roles.console: none documented for developer-console collaborators; workspace roles are managed via custom roles and invites.
roles.customer: A workspace admin who creates a machine user and a least-privilege API key and shares the key with you.

testing: Use your own Plain workspace or trial with a machine user key.

blockers.fix: Tell the customer to copy it before leaving the page.

blockers.problem: Own-workspace OAuth is not usable across customers
GraphQL subscriptions do not accept OAuth tokens

blockers.fix: Read the error and have the customer add the named permission.

automation.agentCan: Write the key intake, GraphQL client and permission-checking code, and draft customer setup instructions.
automation.humanMust: The customer admin creates the machine user and key; you contact Plain for any OAuth or partner options.

uncertain: Roles needed to create machine users and keys; refresh token and default access token lifetimes; whether an OAuth app can be authorized from another workspace (docs imply not); developer.plain.com was blocked by robots rules, so I used www.plain.com docs.
